new.title: De-lensing cosmic birefringence with joint reconstruction
new.summary: Reconstruction of anisotropic cosmic birefringence from the CMB is limited by lensing $B$-mode sample variance and partially degenerate with the lensing curl. We study the joint reconstruction of lensing (gradient and curl) and birefringence at the maximum-a-posteriori point, whose spectra are near-optimal statistics. We predict the joint response and noise analytically, validate them on simulations, and show unbiased inference of its amplitude. Errors will shrink $5$-fold relative to quadratic estimators at SPT-3G+ depths, promising much tighter constraints on parity-violating new physics, owing to the removal of the lensing $B$-polarization sample variance.

new.title: The formation of the first cosmic structures in hybrid Milgromian cosmology
new.summary:
Tackling cosmology with Milgromian Dynamics (MOND) has been a challenge ever since its theoretical inception. In a hybrid MOND scheme, a hypothesized light sterile neutrino of $\approx$ 11 eV/$c^2$ rest-mass is able to provide realistic initial conditions, fitting the third peak of the Planck CMB power spectrum as a Hot Dark Matter (HDM) component. At the same time, MOND governs the gravitational dynamics of density perturbations, while the background expansion follows the standard FLRW metric. We conduct and analyze hydrodynamical simulations of the fiducial $\Lambda$CDM model ($H_0 = 67.8$ km/s/Mpc, $\Omega_m \approx 0.31$, $\Omega_{	ext{CDM}} \approx 0.26$), the progenitor $
u$HDM model ($H_0 = 67.64$ km/s/Mpc, $\Omega_m = 0.3, \Omega_{
u}\approx 0.26$), and its optimized version (opt-$
u$HDM model, $H_0 \approx 55.6$ km/s/Mpc, $\Omega_m \approx 0.49$, $\Omega_{
u} \approx 0.42$), utilizing the publicly available codes RAMSES and Phantom of RAMSES. We compare for the first time the total matter power spectrum $P(k)$ of the hydrodynamical simulations at various redshifts, examining the systematic differences of the three investigated cosmologies. The redshift evolution of the power spectrum of the $\Lambda$CDM model compared to the $
u$HDM variants' counterpart offers important insight about the onset of structure formation. The combination of a light sterile neutrino and MOND gravity exceeds the $\Lambda$CDM model's matter $P(k)$ over all collapsing scales at late times ($z\lesssim 1$). The density and velocity fields reveal a distinct difference between the underlying laws of gravity. Regardless of the modeled dependence in the jointly estimated data from Planck, DES Y1, SDSS, and eBOSS, the $
u$HDM hybrid models seem to produce an excess of power at associated resolution scales due to their cosmological design.

new.title: 3D dark matter map of the JWST COSMOS-Web field using diffusion-based generative priors
new.summary: Mapping the three-dimensional distribution of dark matter is key to tracing the growth of cosmic structure. Two-dimensional weak lensing mass maps recover its projected distribution, but they blend structures at different distances along the line of sight. We reconstruct the three-dimensional matter distribution in the 0.54 deg$^2$ COSMOS-Web field using deep James Webb Space Telescope imaging, with an effective source density of 121 galaxies arcmin$^{-2}$ We combine a physical weak lensing forward model with a diffusion-based Bayesian generative prior learned from cosmological simulations, yielding a posterior distribution of the matter field across 20 lens planes to $z \simeq 2$, doubling the redshift reach of previous Hubble Space Telescope-based 3D reconstructions and approaching cosmic noon, an epoch of rapid galaxy growth. The reconstruction separates structures that overlap in projection and recovers non-Gaussian matter structure across a range of spatial scales, including over-densities associated with independently identified galaxy clusters that were not detected in earlier weak lensing maps. Posterior sampling quantifies the range of three-dimensional matter distributions allowed by the data, enabling a probabilistic visualization of the cosmic web while propagating uncertainties in its inferred structure. Null and simulation-based tests show that the recovered structures are supported by the lensing signal and are consistent with expectations from the fiducial $\Lambda$CDM cosmology. These results extend three-dimensional weak lensing mapping into the high-redshift, non-Gaussian regime and establish a route towards probabilistic mapping of the evolving cosmic web with current wide-field lensing surveys.

new.title: Measuring the ultraviolet background at $z\simeq3$ from the quasar proximity effect in DESI DR1
new.summary: Ionizing radiation from quasars reduces the abundance of neutral hydrogen in the surrounding intergalactic medium (IGM), suppressing Ly$\alpha$ absorption. This absorption deficit, known as the quasar proximity effect, can be used to measure the ultraviolet background (UVBG). We measure the hydrogen photoionization rate of the UVBG in Data Release 1 of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Our sample contains 6,245 quasars over $2.75\leq z<3.25$, selected with rest-frame absolute magnitudes at 1450 Angstroms of $M_{1450}\leq-25.5$ and signal-to-noise ratios of at least 3 measured redward of Ly$\alpha$. We reconstruct quasar continua with principal component analysis trained on Hubble Space Telescope spectra and stack the resulting transmitted-flux profiles. We fit the resulting stacked profile with a halo model that accounts for reduced absorption from quasar radiation and enhanced absorption in the surrounding overdense environment. We constrain the environmental contribution using independent measurements of quasar clustering bias, while the transmission profile constrains the UVBG. To validate our method, we construct mock spectra matched to the luminosity and noise properties of our DESI sample using the Astrid hydrodynamical simulation at $z=3$. We apply the same analysis pipeline to the mock spectra and DESI data, testing the recovery of known input photoionization rates and using the results to calibrate the final UVBG measurement. We obtain $\Gamma_{\mathrm{HI}}=(1.376^{+0.095}_{-0.076})\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ at $z\simeq3$. The statistical errors are obtained by bootstrap resampling the DESI sightlines. We also estimate a systematic uncertainty of $^{+0.837}_{-0.521}\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

new.title: Stress-Testing Small-Scale Cosmological Inference With Empirical Galaxy--Halo Connection Models
new.summary: Small-scale galaxy clustering contains substantial cosmological information, but extracting it reliably requires robust modeling of the galaxy--halo connection. In this work, we compare two widely adopted families of empirical models, subhalo abundance matching (SHAM) and the halo occupation distribution (HOD), testing their predictions for galaxy clustering and their recovery of the input cosmology. Using Aemulus-$\beta$, a new multi-cosmology simulation suite with substructure merger trees, we fit multiple SHAM and HOD models to the small-scale clustering of a stellar-mass-selected mock galaxy catalog generated with the more physical semi-empirical model UniverseMachine. We then use cosmological evidence modeling to infer the structure growth parameter $S_8$. Our results show that the SHAM model, regardless of the treatment of numerically disrupted subhalos, is able to offer tight, unbiased constraints on $S_8$ with ~2-3% precision, using simulations of relatively small volumes that span a limited number of cosmologies. In contrast, HOD models, even when accounting for assembly bias, yield weaker and potentially biased cosmological constraints that are sensitive to implementation choices: the inferred $S_8$ degrades in precision to ~6-11% and can be offset by ~1$\sigma$. This suggests that the excessive parametric flexibility and model misspecification of most commonly adopted HOD models can degrade and bias the resulting cosmological constraints. We further evaluate each model's performance in predicting higher-order statistics not used in the fit and find that SHAM generally reproduces them more accurately than the tested HOD models. These results highlight the potential of leveraging predictive subhalo-level information from simulations to enable robust cosmological inference on small scales.

new.title: Structural axes of sources in the SUMSS survey and their alignments
new.summary: Coherent orientations of extragalactic radio sources have been reported on large angular scales, but their statistical significance and susceptibility to observational systematics remain debated. Searches based on very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) also leave the far southern sky comparatively sparsely sampled. We test for local alignments of kiloparsec-scale radio source structural axes in the Sydney University Molonglo Sky Survey (SUMSS), providing a complementary probe in the undersampled southern sky. We constructed a catalog of structural position angles for 4087 sources from 629 SUMSS mosaics. A convolutional neural network supplied initial angle estimates, which were corrected for image-to-sky coordinate distortion and visually vetted. We searched for local alignments using a coordinate-invariant parallel transport statistic on HEALPix tessellations, then refined candidate regions with a genetic algorithm. We calibrated the significance of the full search against mock skies that preserve the declination-dependent position angle distribution and undergo the same search procedure. Several regions show apparently strong local alignment, but none remains statistically significant after accounting for the look-elsewhere effect. The candidate signals are consistent with chance fluctuations in the full search. We find no statistically significant evidence for alignment of structural axes of radio sources in SUMSS images. The resulting southern sky position angle catalog provides a useful resource for future studies of radio source morphology and population properties.

new.title: Reconstructing the Large-Scale Velocity Field from DESI DR1 with Bayesian Inference
new.summary: Survey boundaries and nonlinear dynamics complicate reconstruction of large-scale matter-density and peculiar-velocity fields from galaxy redshift surveys. We develop and compare two reconstruction methods within a common Bayesian framework, based on linear perturbation theory and the Zel'dovich approximation, and apply them to the DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey. We infer the initial density field using a Gaussian prior and likelihood, with the Zel'dovich model displacing particles from a uniform Lagrangian grid. Both yield maximum a posteriori (MAP) fields; only the linear posterior is sampled. Our main findings are: \textit{(i)} Both reconstructions yield similar large-scale density structures and coherent velocity patterns in the survey interior, beyond roughly \(50\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}\) from the footprint boundaries. \textit{(ii)} Comparison with Cosmicflows-4 groups, predominantly from the SDSS Fundamental Plane sample in the DESI overlap, shows close agreement between mean observed radial velocities and MAP predictions when binned by the latter, despite substantial individual scatter. \textit{(iii)} Both yield similar reflex-dipole profiles, defined as mean shell velocities relative to those at randomly sampled centres, out to \(\sim225\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}\). The profiles depend weakly on the prior normalization \(\sigma_8\), but lie below the fiducial linear \(\Lambda\)CDM reference at \(r<50\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}\). Sparse sampling limits the largest radii. \textit{(iv)} In an exploratory BAO test, shifting galaxies and randoms to a target redshift \(z=8\) using reconstructed displacements sharpens the acoustic feature in both cases, with a slightly more pronounced peak for Zel'dovich. Survey geometry and galaxy bias remain the principal limitations.

new.title: Linear perturbation theory and structure formation in a Horndeski theory of gravity without dark matter
new.summary: We study the formation and evolution of the cosmic large-scale structure (LSS) in a scalar-tensor Horndeski theory of gravity without dark matter. We impose that this theory reduces to Refracted Gravity (RG) in the weak-field limit. RG is a non-relativistic theory where the gravitational permittivity $\epsilon(\rho)$, with $\rho$ the baryonic matter density, provides the gravitational boost required to describe both the dynamics of galaxies and galaxy clusters without dark matter. We show that $\epsilon(\rho)$ equals the function $G_4(\varphi)$ of the scalar field $\varphi$ of our Horndeski model. The background evolution of a flat, matter-dominated, homogeneous and isotropic universe shows that $\varphi$ is also responsible for the accelerated expansion of the universe and that the model is capable of reproducing the observed redshift evolution of the Hubble-Lemaître parameter. We finally develop the linear perturbation theory and study the growth factor equation. The model fails to correctly describe the LSS by predicting a late onset of the formation of cosmic structure at redshift $z\lesssim 1$.

new.title: Cosmological evolution and late-time attractors in axion-monopole interacting dark energy
new.summary: We investigate the cosmological dynamics of axion-monopole interacting dark energy, examining whether a microscopically motivated dark-sector interaction can sustain stable late-time acceleration. In particular, magnetic monopoles constitute dark matter and an ultralight axion contributes to dark energy, with their interaction arising from the Witten effect through field-dependent dyon masses. We formulate the autonomous system, classify its critical points and stability, and investigate the evolution analytically and numerically. We find that stable de Sitter attractors at finite positive Hubble parameter require a positive cosmological constant and correspond to axion-potential minima, whereas those at maxima are unstable. Nevertheless, transient axion-driven acceleration remains possible without an explicit cosmological constant. Furthermore, the interaction induces matter-era tracking, namely an attracting slow-drift regime rather than an exact critical point. The interaction-effective dark-energy equation of state can cross the phantom divide, although the physical equation of state remains non-phantom. Extending the analysis to the full Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield dyon mass, we find that the main dynamical features persist, while the field evolution and interaction strength depend on the microscopic dyon properties. Our results demonstrate how a microscopically motivated dark-sector interaction can give rise to distinctive cosmological evolution and effective dark-energy behavior.

new.title: Bright Siren Cosmology Beyond Fisher: DALI Forecasts for Third-Generation Gravitational Wave Observatories
new.summary: In this work we assess non-Gaussian extensions of Fisher forecasting based on the Derivative Approximation for Likelihoods (DALI). We simulate ensembles of bright siren catalogs for third-generation observatories, adopting a Cosmic Explorer (CE) and a triangular Einstein Telescope (ET) network, frequency-domain inspiral waveforms, and selection-motivated priors for counterpart detection. We reconstruct approximate likelihoods using Fisher and the first DALI correction (Doublet), and propagate the inferred distance information to cosmological inference in a w0waCDM model. We find that the Doublet approximation provides tighter cosmological constraints than the Fisher approximation, reducing the inferred uncertainties by approximately a factor of two in agreement with non-approximate likelihood (called Exact) results. For our GW network onfiguration, 300 bright-siren detections up to z=1 yield an H0 precision of ~2.7% with the Doublet approximation, compared with ~2.5% for the exact likelihood. The adopted non-Gaussian GW priors induce a systematic displacement of the inferred luminosity distances from the fiducial values, which is also present in the exact GW reconstruction and propagates into the cosmological parameters. Compared with the exact cosmological likelihood, the Doublet results differ by only ~10% on average in the parameter uncertainties, compared with ~195% for the traditional Fisher approximation. The Doublet approximation also substantially reduces the computational cost, by a factor of ~55 for the GW analysis and by ~12 for cosmological likelihood evaluations, yielding an estimated reduction of ~55 in the total computational cost of the combined analysis. Our results show the potential of DALI-based approximations to provide accurate and computationally efficient tools for forecasting in bright siren cosmology.

new.title: Mapping large-scale structure without galaxy formation - combining fast radio bursts with CMB lensing
new.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are an emerging precision probe of cosmological fluctuations. The amount and quality of observed FRB data will grow enormously over the next decade. FRB dispersion data directly probe the free electron distribution up to intergalactic scales. Precision models of the free electron distribution are necessary to exploit this exciting new probe of large-scale structure. We show that the free electron distribution almost exactly follows the total matter distribution. We confirm this fact by estimating the electron field-level bias parameters for the first time from the FLAMINGO simulations. With simulation-based knowledge of a handful of electron free parameters, the electron distribution largely acts as a second realization of the matter distribution. Working on large scales, we can leverage this fact to combine FRB correlations with those of Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) weak lensing to constrain cosmological parameters. Assuming access to localized FRBs with redshifts, we perform cosmological forecasts using these two large-scale matter probes, which have no strong dependence on baryonic feedback models nor on parameters that encode galaxy formation. We show that the parameters $\sigma_8$ and $\Omega_m$ are constrained at a level similar to or better than that obtained by combining FRB dispersion with weak lensing of galaxy shapes under conservative assumptions. These results motivate the use of FRB data as a complementary probe of cosmic structure and will be especially compelling as redshifts become available for localized FRB host galaxies.

new.title: SBi3PCF: cosmology with Dark Energy Survey Year 3 cosmic shear
new.summary: We present the first cosmic shear data analysis of the integrated 3-point correlation function (i3PCF), a higher-order weak lensing statistic, and the first simulation-based inference (SBI) analysis of a three-point cosmic shear correlation function on survey data. Using SBi3PCF, our previously developed SBI framework for the i3PCF, we jointly constrain the $w$CDM parameter space with the cosmic shear 2-point correlation functions $\xi_\pm$ (2PCFs) and the i3PCFs $\zeta_\pm$ from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3) weak lensing shape catalogue, from which we detect $\zeta_\pm$ with a signal-to-noise ratio of 12.8. Our forward model is built on the CosmoGridV1 N-body simulations and includes the survey mask, shape noise, intrinsic alignment, baryonic feedback, photometric redshift uncertainty and shear calibration bias. The analysis was carried out blind, with all choices frozen, and only unblinded once coverage tests, tests of the accuracy of the learned likelihoods, and internal consistency tests had been passed. For the joint $\xi_\pm$ + $\zeta_\pm$ analysis we obtain $\Omega_m = 0.272^{+0.038}_{-0.033}$, $S_8 = 0.784^{+0.024}_{-0.021}$ and $w_0 = -1.04^{+0.25}_{-0.19}$. Adding $\zeta_\pm$ improves the figure of merit in the $\Omega_m$-$S_8$-$w_0$ parameter space by a factor of $1.59$ over $\xi_\pm$ alone, as predicted by simulated i3PCF analyses. This gain comes from third-order information on angular scales $\geq 15'$ and aperture radii $\geq 50'$, a regime where baryonic effects are subdominant. The constraints are consistent with the other DES Y3 analyses of the same catalogue and with independent lensing analyses, and differ by at most $2.4\sigma$ from CMB and BAO data (Planck 2018 + BAO, in $\Omega_m$-$S_8$-$w_0$). This shows that $\zeta_\pm$ can be analysed on cosmological survey data with a fully simulation-based approach, an important step towards Stage-IV surveys.

cross.title: Gauge-invariant non-universal scalar couplings in teleparallel gravity
cross.summary: We develop a gauge-invariant teleparallel framework in which the universality of the gravitational coupling is relaxed for a scalar field, while the gravitational sector retains the form of the teleparallel equivalent of General Relativity. The non-universal interaction is encoded in a scalar-sector tetrad whose coupling to the universal translational gauge potential is controlled by a field-dependent gravitational charge. A Stückelberg completion preserves local translational gauge invariance, and we derive the gravitational, scalar-field, and Stückelberg equations, together with the antisymmetric constraint and their consistency relations. As a first application, we investigate homogeneous and isotropic cosmology, where the Stückelberg constraint provides a first integral governing the evolution of the non-universal coupling. In the kination-dominated regime, the standard stiff-fluid behavior is recovered asymptotically, whereas in the potential-dominated regime, accelerated expansion requires additional conditions beyond potential domination. We identify compatible expanding solutions in which departures from universality are dynamically suppressed, including examples approaching power-law inflation or asymptotically de Sitter expansion. Including a universally coupled perfect fluid and a constant scalar potential, we obtain a late-time solution exhibiting a subdominant matter-like contribution to the background Friedmann equation and an asymptotic de Sitter limit. These results provide a gauge-theoretic realization of non-universal scalar couplings and highlight their potential implications for early- and late-time cosmology.

cross.title: Cosmic-Ray Signals from Dark Matter Annihilation into Scalars with Baryon Number
cross.summary: Cosmic-ray antideuterons and antihelium-3 nuclei are promising probes of dark matter (DM). In light of potential detections of heavy antinuclei at AMS-02, we investigate a recently proposed scenario in which DM annihilates into color-singlet scalars carrying baryon and lepton number, which has been shown to enhance antideuteron and antihelium-3 fluxes relative to antiprotons. Accounting for Galactic propagation and detector sensitivities, we calculate the number of events predicted by our model for parameters that are compatible with the seven-year AMS-02 antiproton data. Broad regions of the DM-mediator mass plane result in observable antideuteron fluxes at AMS-02 and GAPS. While detecting antihelium-3 remains more challenging, potentially detectable fluxes can arise for light mediators and moderately light DM, and in general are enhanced relative to the standard WIMP predictions. Furthermore, we find antihelium-to-antideuteron event ratios of O(0.1), closer to those suggested by the reported AMS-02 candidate events than conventional WIMP predictions.

cross.title: Ly$α$ in Compact Broad-Line Emitters, Including Little Red Dots, Is More Closely Linked to the Host Galaxy than to the Broad-Line Nucleus
cross.summary: JWST has found many faint broad-line AGN at $z>4$, but it is unclear whether the Ly$\alpha$ we see from them comes from the accreting black hole or from its host galaxy. The answer matters for how these sources are interpreted and for how many ionizing photons they release. We use deep JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy from the DIVER program to measure Ly$\alpha$ in 12 compact broad-line emitters (CBEs) at $z=4.2$--5.5 in GOODS-N. CBEs include little red dots (LRDs), little blue dots, and other broad-line AGN. Six are detected in Ly$\alpha$. Every source shows a broad-line region, yet Ly$\alpha$ does not follow it: the sources with the strongest H$\alpha$ relative to the UV include weak detections and nondetections, and every detected Ly$\alpha$ line (FWHM $\approx300$--1000~km~s$^{-1}$) is narrower than broad H$\alpha$ (1100--3300~km~s$^{-1}$). Instead, Ly$\alpha$ appears to track the host galaxy. We model the AGN-subtracted host with a dust-attenuated SED fit. Including the upper limits, the observed Ly$\alpha$ follows the Ly$\alpha$ production in this host model more closely than it follows H$\alpha$/UV, in both equivalent width and luminosity. Every detection exceeds its host-model value by a factor of 1.5--18, leaving room for a nuclear contribution. The black hole is visible in these sources, but the Ly$\alpha$ we observe is more closely tied to its host. The median effective Ly$\alpha$ escape fraction of the detections is only 0.09, which suggests that ionizing escape from CBEs is typically modest and varies widely.

cross.title: A full chemical network treatment of supermassive black hole seed formation from dark matter annihilation or decay
cross.summary: The recent discoveries of high-redshift quasars at $z\sim6-10.1$ present a challenge to conventional supermassive black hole (SMBH) formation scenarios: their central SMBHs are too large to have grown from early stellar remnants, even under efficient super-Eddington accretion. An alternative approach is the direct collapse of primordial, dust- and metal-free gas clouds into black hole seeds as early as $z\sim20$. To prevent fragmentation from highly efficient molecular hydrogen cooling and allow such a collapse, a strong flux of UV photons is required to photodissociate molecular hydrogen, suppressing star formation. We investigate whether the decay or annihilation of dark matter with masses below $\sim200$ eV can produce sufficient UV radiation, both from the cosmological background and within early dark matter halos. Using thermal simulations of a one-zone primordial gas cloud model with the Grackle chemistry and cooling library, we map the resulting gas behavior across a range of dark matter lifetimes, cross sections, and masses. From this, we determine regions of parameter space where direct collapse into an SMBH is possible and the corresponding maximum halo mass required.

cross.title: Presupernovae Strongly Constrain Electrophilic MeV Bosons
cross.summary: The years preceding a supernova (SN) can constrain new electrophilic bosons with MeV masses more than the explosion itself. Although cooler than SNe, the massive progenitors maintain consistently high temperatures much longer, injecting more particles whose decays to positrons contribute to the diffuse Galactic 511-keV emission. For dark photons, the increase is exacerbated by the lower plasma frequency compared to SNe, where MeV excitations are screened. We find preSNe bounds on dark photon couplings up to two orders of magnitude stronger than SNe for masses between 1 and 3~MeV, with similar improvements for other electrophilic species such as axion-like particles.

cross.title: Towards Self-consistent Modeling of Quasi-Stars and their NLTE Spectra: Implications for Little Red Dots
cross.summary: Quasi-stars, massive envelopes surrounding rapidly accreting black hole (BH) seeds, are promising candidates for explaining the rapid formation of supermassive black holes in the early Universe and may account for some of the JWST-discovered Little Red Dots (LRDs). We present a self-consistent framework combining stellar evolution calculations with non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) spectral synthesis to test this connection. Our models drop the polytropic assumptions of previous work: the envelope is described entirely by mixing-length theory, with saturated convection and radiative energy setting the luminosity at an inner boundary a few hundred Schwarzschild radii from the BH. This removes the BH-mass limits of earlier models, and we follow the evolution up to BH-to-total mass ratios approaching unity. We then use TLUSTY to compute the first converged NLTE atmospheric models for the surface conditions and primordial hydrogen-helium composition expected in quasi-stars. Our models produce cool photospheres, prominent Balmer breaks, and Balmer and Paschen absorption features. NLTE effects substantially modify line strengths, increasing Balmer absorption depths by $\sim 35-55\%$ relative to LTE models, while having a minor effect on the continuum. Comparison with observed LRD spectral energy distributions shows broad agreement in continuum shape, although our models do not reproduce their commonly observed strong emission lines. Under the quasi-star interpretation, comparisons with individual LRDs suggest characteristic quasi-star masses of approximately $10^5-10^7 M_\odot$. These results establish a physically motivated connection between quasi-star evolution and observable spectra, providing a framework for testing quasi-stars as progenitors of LRDs while identifying limitations of current atmospheric models.

cross.title: Latin hypercube sampling to reduce the variance in Monte Carlo integration: a practical guide and an application to gravitational-wave astronomy
cross.summary: In applied statistics, likelihoods involving high-dimensional integrals are often approximated via Monte Carlo summation. Controlling the resulting numerical variance is crucial for reliable inference. We provide a practical introduction to Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) and its extension based on orthogonal arrays (OA-LHS) as strategies to reduce this variance by stratifying the sampling distribution. LHS asymptotically removes variance contributions from individual coordinates, while strength-2 OA-LHS also removes those from pairwise interactions, yielding orders-of-magnitude improvements over plain Monte Carlo estimators for suitable integrands. As a case study, we investigate their application to the selection function entering hierarchical inference of gravitational-wave populations. At approximately one million injections, we find only a marginal reduction in variance, with low statistical significance. Nevertheless, the computational cost of constructing these designs is negligible relative to evaluating gravitational-wave injections, making even marginal gains worth considering for future applications. This practical introduction to LHS and OA-LHS offers a starting point for other applications in physics and astronomy involving computationally expensive Monte Carlo calculations.

cross.title: Comment on "Long-range magnetic fields in the ground state of the Standard Model plasma"
cross.summary: We revisit the two-loop parity-odd photon polarization analyzed by Boyarsky, Ruchayskiy, and Shaposhnikov [Phys. Rev. Lett. 109, 111602 (2012)]. The original calculation neglected opposite- fermion-flow partner diagrams for the tadpole and exchange-bubble topologies alike. We quantify the impact of the properly restored exchange-bubble coefficients on the static magnetic response.

cross.title: Gravitational-wave lensing beyond the diffraction integral: proper-time methods and the bound lens
cross.summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) can have wavelengths comparable to the Schwarzschild radius of their lenses, and detectors record their phase, so lensing requires wave optics. Its standard tool, the diffraction integral, follows from the particle path integral of a scalar wave on a static weak field, under the eikonal (one-way) and paraxial approximations, plus the thin-lens limit. We give a self-contained account of how the proper-time (worldline) representation overcomes these steps. An auxiliary proper time makes the wave equation exactly first order, with frequency as $1/\hbar$, so geometric optics and, for paraxial thin-lens paths, the diffraction integral follow from stationarity of an exact integral. For a point mass, the Duru-Kleinert (DK) gauge and Kustaanheimo-Stiefel map give the exact propagator; for a distant observer the DK time and fibre angle become the radius and azimuth of a lens plane, the result is the point-lens amplification factor with the offset set by the excess path, and geometric optics requires $w\gg1$ and $wy\gg1$. This agreement reflects the Coulomb potential, not the approximations: the exact eikonal condition, $\varepsilon_E\simeq\bar\lambda/d+GM/c^2d+\mathcal O(\sin^2\theta/2)$, fails near the lens and at large angles, and the one-way step is a non-relativistic limit. We then treat the bound lens, a GW source orbiting its lens, which emits a backscattered echo and moves during the lensing delays. Its exact time-domain signal gives each worldline its own retarded time and Doppler factor, so no single amplification factor describes it. In the diffraction regime the Shapiro phase alone misses all lensing beyond it, geometric optics misses 46-100% of it near conjunction at $w=0.3$, the paraxial geometry fails on the far side, and the static amplification factor along the orbit errs by $\approx(1-2)\,wM/R$ near conjunction and by the echo amplitude elsewhere.

cross.title: Macrocanonical Generator Networks: Data-Efficient Neural Surrogates for Amortized Physics Simulation
cross.summary: Many scientific simulations are computationally expensive, limiting their use in simulation-based inference, uncertainty quantification, and decision making. We introduce macrocanonical generator networks, a framework for learning fast, data-efficient neural surrogates for amortized simulation of stationary physical processes by matching multiscale statistics of a target process. Inspired by microcanonical maximum-entropy synthesis, which matches feature statistics per sample by inner-loop optimization, our approach instead trains a neural generator to satisfy the same constraints in expectation, preserving physically realistic sample-to-sample fluctuations. We prove that gradient-descent training induces preconditioned gradient-descent dynamics in sample space that inherit the symmetry-preservation properties of the microcanonical gradient descent of Bruna and Mallat, amortizing its per-sample inner-loop optimization into a single training run after which every sample is generated in one forward pass. We further show that residual generator parameterizations initialized near the identity, trained with a small learning rate, preserve entropy locally during early optimization and mitigate mode collapse. Experiments on cosmology and fluid simulations show that macrocanonical generators recover realistic samples from extremely small training sets, in some cases a single training example, while generating new realizations more than $10^6$ times faster per sample than the reference simulator and more than $10^3$ times faster than microcanonical gradient descent. The trained generators can be reused for downstream pretraining, including simulation-based inference, providing a data-efficient route to multi-fidelity scientific machine learning workflows.

repl.title: Universality of Primordial Anisotropies in Gravitational Wave Background
repl.summary: We investigate the general structure of primordial anisotropies in the stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB). Many mechanisms generating primordial SGWB anisotropies, including fossil and propagation effects, exhibit similar multipole dependences despite their distinct physical origins, implying the presence of a common underlying structure. To characterize this structure, we introduce a model-independent framework, the Cosmological Form Factor (CFF), that describes how long-wavelength perturbations modulate short-scale SGWB statistics. Within this broad class of mechanisms, we show that the allowed angular and polarization structures of SGWB anisotropies are universally determined by general principles, including statistical isotropy, locality, and the basic properties of long-wavelength perturbations. In contrast to these universal structures, observables such as amplitudes and frequency dependence retain information about the origin. Our results provide a unified and effective description of primordial SGWB anisotropies, clarifying which aspects are universal and which are model dependent, and therefore offer a theoretical foundation for interpreting future gravitational-wave observations.

repl.title: CMB Spectral Distortions from Resonant Conversions in Atomic Dark Sectors
repl.summary: Dark sectors consisting of atomic constituents (electrons, protons, and photons) offer a well-motivated extension to the Standard Model while providing multiple avenues for phenomenological study. In this work, we explore the impact of conversions between the dark and Standard Model photons in the primordial CMB spectral distortion epoch ($10^3 \lesssim z \lesssim 10^6$). These conversions are resonantly enhanced when the induced thermal masses of both photonic species are equal, thus leading to the possibility that sizeable distortions can be produced. To this end, we solve the Boltzmann equation at early times to determine the (irreducible) freeze-in or freeze-out abundance of dark photons. This procedure also allows us to update the limits on generic milli-charged dark sectors using the ACT DR6 bound on the number of effective radiative degrees of freedom ($N_{\rm eff}$). By then modeling the evolution of the thermal masses in both sectors, we compute the primordial CMB distortion using the Landau-Zener formalism. We find that when the dark electron and proton are roughly similar in mass (the positronium limit), current spectral distortion data from the COBE/FIRAS instrument is able to rule out novel regions of parameter space. We also forecast bounds from the proposed FOSSIL satellite, finding that spectral distortions can also be used to probe the ultra-low dark electric charge regions of parameter space, which are difficult to investigate by other means.

repl.title: Cosmology of Inelastic Self-Interacting Dark Matter: Linear Evolution and Observational Constraints
repl.summary: We study the linear cosmological evolution of inelastic self-interacting dark matter in a two-component dark sector with a small mass splitting, assuming thermal initial conditions for the two species. We derive the coupled background and perturbation equations for inelastic conversion between the two species, considering both power-law and low-velocity saturation cross sections. Exothermic conversion injects kinetic energy into the light component, generating pressure support that suppresses small-scale structure and produces dark acoustic oscillations in the matter power spectrum. The resulting cutoff at scale $k > 1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ depends on the normalization and velocity dependence of the cross section, the dark matter mass and the mass splitting. Using linear power spectra computed with a modified Boltzmann solver, we apply recast constraints from Lyman-$\alpha$ forest data and high-redshift UV luminosity functions, finding non-monotonic but closed exclusion regions driven by the competition between efficient conversion and rapid depletion of the heavy component. These results show that the internal thermodynamics of a secluded multi-component dark sector can leave observable imprints on structure formation, providing a complementary probe of secluded dark matter.

repl.title: Eigenvalue formulation of Stochastic Inflation and application to large perturbation generating inflationary features
repl.summary: Stochastic inflation is a powerful technique for calculating the probability distribution function (PDF) of large inflationary perturbations, which may collapse to form Primordial Black Holes. The PDF, $P({\cal N})$, of the stochastic number of e-folds, ${\cal N}$, satisfies an adjoint Fokker-Planck Equation. We develop a new self-contained eigenvalue technique which can be used to determine $P({\cal N})$. First we apply this method to the simple case of quantum diffusion along a flat potential without any classical drift. We recover the expression for the PDF that has previously been found using characteristic functions, with an exponential tail, and a power-law behaviour, $P({\cal N}) \propto {\cal N}^{-3/2}$, in the intermediate regime between the peak and the tail of the PDF. Finally we apply the method to constant drift inflation, in the narrow- and broad-well limits. In the narrow-well limit, there is an analytic solution and the PDF is similar to the drift-free case, with a mildly suppressed tail. In the broad-well limit, determining the full set of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions requires a piecewise construction of the spectrum, and the broad-well PDF is qualitatively different, with an enhanced peak and a strongly suppressed tail.

repl.title: Memoirs of the curvaton: non-perturbative non-Gaussianity and supermassive primordial black holes
repl.summary: The curvaton provides a simple mechanism for generating strongly non-Gaussian curvature perturbations after inflation, with potentially important consequences on small scales. We study curvaton dynamics beyond the standard quadratic potential and construct the local non-Gaussian map $\zeta=F(\zeta_{\rm G})$ relating the curvature perturbation to an auxiliary Gaussian field $\zeta_{\rm G}$. Curvaton self-interactions make the onset of oscillations field dependent and modify the effective equation of state once the curvaton enters the adiabatic regime. We incorporate these effects using the abbreviated action, which provides a compact way to connect the frozen and oscillatory regimes and exposes sources of non-Gaussianity absent in the purely quadratic case. We apply the formalism to quadratic, monomial, quartic, and cosine potentials, for which we derive the mapping $F(\zeta_{\rm G})$ and show that self-interactions can either enhance or suppress the resulting non-Gaussianity depending on the potential and initial conditions. We consider non-perturbative aspects in the strongly non-Gaussian regime, and show how strong non-Gaussianity can suppress the power spectrum. As an application, we provide a bottom-up scenario in which strongly positive curvaton non-Gaussianity allows primordial supermassive black hole seeds at peak amplitudes $\mathcal{A}_\textrm{pk}\sim10^{-3}$, which are compatible with the COBE/FIRAS $\mu$-distortion bounds. This opens a new primordial scenario for the Little Red Dots observed by the JWST. The axion-like curvaton provides a particularly natural setting for this mechanism.

repl.title: Can cosmic voids ease the Hubble tension? Local expansion in $w_0w_a$CDM
repl.summary: We investigate the effect of local cosmic voids on low-redshift measurements of the Hubble rate in flat $w_0w_a$CDM cosmologies. Using a hydrodynamical model for isolated spherical inverse top-hat underdensities, we compute the void-induced Hubble shift as a function of redshift, enclosed density contrast $\delta_{\rm E}$ and cosmological parameters. We find that the effect is mainly controlled by the matter sector, through $\delta_{\rm E}$ and $\Omega_{\rm m,0}$, while dynamical dark energy gives only subdominant late-time corrections. For a Planck-calibrated $\Lambda$CDM background, matching the SH0ES value requires a present-day void with $\delta_{\rm E}(z=0)\simeq -0.44$, substantially deeper than the KBC-like local underdensity. A KBC-like void lowers the SH0ES-Planck discrepancy to about $2\sigma$, but is not deep enough to fully reconcile the two measurements. Allowing for dynamical dark energy, including regions motivated by recent DES and DESI analyses, changes this result only at the percent level. We also show that the reported redshift dependence of locally inferred $H_0$ values can be represented phenomenologically by an effective enclosed matter profile. This reconstruction should be interpreted as a consistency test of local-structure effects rather than as explanation for an evolving background value of $H_0$. Overall, local underdensities can affect low-redshift Hubble-rate inferences, but they do not resolve the Hubble tension within the spherical void setup considered here.

repl.title: Gravitational waves from super-Hubble bubbles
repl.summary: We consider a cosmological first-order phase transition in which bubbles of true vacuum nucleate during inflation but do not collide and percolate until the Universe has entered the radiation-dominated era. If the collisions take place soon after the end of inflation, the size of these bubbles can be significantly greater than the Hubble length. This has two important consequences for the gravitational waves produced by the bubble collisions: First, as the peak frequency is determined by the comoving bubble radius, it can be well below the MHz frequencies typical for bubble collisions at the end of inflation. Second, when comparing collisions beginning at the same time, the amplitude of the gravitational waves is greatly enhanced relative to Hubble-sized and smaller bubbles. Together, these two effects mean that gravitational waves produced by super-Hubble bubbles soon after the end of inflation can be within the observable frequency and amplitude ranges of LIGO and NANOGrav, as well as LISA and other future gravitational wave experiments. We demonstrate this with a simple illustrative model.

repl.title: Sample Variance Cancellation for Future Spectroscopic Surveys
repl.summary: High-redshift spectroscopic galaxy surveys will be the scientific engines of the next generation of large-scale structure cosmology. The clustering signal of high redshift, star-forming Lyman-$\alpha$ emitters (LAEs) will be of key importance for obtaining high-redshift constraints on the growth of structure and redshift-space distortions. The complex radiative transfer (RT) of Lyman-$\alpha$ photons alters the symmetry group respected by the overdensity field constructed from these galaxies, and so the observed large-scale clustering of LAEs may have an angular dependence that differs significantly from that of linear theory, possibly biasing inference of cosmological parameters. While such an effect has been seen in simulations, its amplitude in nature and its detailed form remains unclear. In the restricted context of a linear, Gaussian model, we outline a procedure for pinning down the type and amplitude of such changes in angular dependence on large scales due to unknown RT or a more general unmodeled angular effect in the hypothetical scenario in which an observer is presented with LAE data containing such an effect. We show that if a second tracer without the modified angular dependence is available for cross correlation with the LAEs at the same redshifts (e.g., Lyman-break galaxies), then, with a high redshift survey of modest size, it is possible to rapidly identify: 1) the presence of a nontrivial angular functional form of radiative transfer (by a conditional field-level realization), 2) the functional form itself (with an optimal filter that we derive), and 3) the value of its amplitude with an uncertainty (via an adaptation of the standard quadratic estimator). Such sample-variance-cancellation strategies therefore provide a statistical solution to unknown astrophysical or systematic angular clustering dependence, including from RT.

repl.title: An Enhanced Isothermal Jeans Approach to Constraining Dark Matter Self-Interactions from Galactic Kinematics
repl.summary: We present an improved semi-analytical model to predict density profiles of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halos and apply it to constrain the self-scattering cross section using SPARC galaxy rotation curves. Building on the isothermal Jeans approach, our model incorporates (i) velocity-dependent cross sections, (ii) an empirical treatment of core collapse, and (iii) enhanced robustness for identifying solutions. These advances allow us to fit a large sample of galaxies, including systems with baryon-dominated centers often excluded in earlier studies. We find that roughly 1/6 of galaxies admit both a core-growth and a core-collapse solution, while the rest favor a unique evolutionary state. Joint constraints across the sample reveal clear velocity dependence: the allowed parameter space forms an L-shaped degeneracy, where both nearly constant, low cross sections ($\sigma_0\sim2\,{\rm cm}^2$/g, $\omega\gtrsim500\,$km/s) and strongly velocity-dependent models ($\sigma_0\sim100\,{\rm cm}^2$/g, $\omega\sim60\,$km/s) are viable. Adopting the core-growth interpretation yields best-fit values $\sigma_0\simeq5\,{\rm cm}^2$/g and $\omega\simeq250\,$km/s. Our constraints are remarkably consistent with previous results derived from a variety of independent probes. Compared to cold dark matter (CDM) models, SIDM outperforms simple adiabatic-contraction profiles and rivals empirical feedback-based CDM profiles, yet shows no correlation with stellar-to-halo mass ratio, a proxy for feedback strength, offering a distinct explanation for dwarf galaxy diversity. Moreover, SIDM does not affect galaxy-halo scaling relations significantly and makes concentration systematically lower. Our results highlight SIDM as a compelling framework for small-scale structure, while future low-mass kinematic data will be crucial for breaking degeneracies in velocity-dependent cross-section models.

repl.title: Dark graviton sensing with magnetically levitated superconductors
repl.summary: Levitated sensors have emerged as a new frontier to detect ultra-light dark matter such as axion-like particles and dark photons. In this work we study how a magnetically levitated superconductor responds to a spin-2 dark matter field, the dark graviton, in the dHz to kHz frequency range. To do so, we compute the forces that the dark graviton exerts on the superconductor, separately for matter and light couplings. The matter coupling produces a strain-like tidal acceleration between the superconductor and the centre of mass of the rigid apparatus, resulting in a displacement relative to the readout pick-up loop, in a way analogous to the response to a slow, continuous, massive gravitational wave. The light coupling instead induces an effective current that sources an oscillating magnetic field, thus driving the superdiamagnetic response of the superconductor. We find that, albeit with significant experimental improvements, the sensitivity reach for the matter coupling could surpass existing fifth-force experiments in the audio frequency band. At the same time, magnetically levitated superconductors could be among the most sensitive laboratory probes of the dark-graviton coupling to electromagnetism, especially at low frequencies, provided technical and readout noise can be kept under control.

repl.title: Particle--antiparticle asymmetry from charge separation at expanding horizons
repl.summary: In a Friedmann universe with a time-varying cosmological term, massive particle--antiparticle pairs are produced continuously from the spacetime vacuum, and their members are separated by horizons. Along the cosmic history that explains $n_s$, $A_s$, $r$ and the low-$\ell$ power anomaly, we show how this separation generates the observed asymmetry. Horizons absorb the charge they separate, since gravity does not conserve global charges. Charge separation at the many horizons inside today's Hubble volume then acts as a volume violation of the U(1) charge, at a rate $\Gamma_C=\kappa_C\Gamma_M$ proportional to pair production. The sign requires a C- and CP-odd coupling to the time arrow. We describe both by an effective Lagrangian with a U(1)-violating coupling $g_c\,\delta\mathcal O_S\Phi^2$ to the spacetime vacuum and a time bias $-\partial_\mu f(R)\,J^\mu$. For $f=c_a\ln|R|$ the chemical potential of producing a particle is $\mu\simeq2c_a\dot H/H$. The asymmetry per pair reaches an attractor in the pair-dominated episode and freezes when the cosmological term is exhausted. The observed value requires $|c_a|/\tau_S\simeq(0.65$--$1.0)\times10^{-4}$, with $T_S=\tau_SH/2\pi$ the temperature of the spacetime vacuum, and its sign is fixed by the arrow of time. The Yukawa decays of the pairs transfer the asymmetry, with a uniform sign, to baryons and leptons and to dark-matter particles. The current of the charged decay products generates a magnetic field of $10^{-14}$--$10^{-11}$ G today on the coherence length of reheating.

repl.title: Opening the Window of Ultra-Light PBHs by Exorcising the Poltergeist
repl.summary: The hot Big Bang may have emerged from evaporation of primordial black holes (PBHs) lighter than $10^9$g. Standard monochromatic treatments predict nearly simultaneous evaporation, abrupt reheating, and a large Poltergeist scalar-induced gravitational wave signal. We confront this expectation with the irreducible collapse mass tail predicted by general relativity, $df_{\rm PBH}/d\ln M\propto M^{3.78}$, which smooths reheating, suppresses the signal by orders of magnitude, and reopens the ultra-light PBH window.

repl.title: Revealing a multi-zone circumnuclear dust response in UGC 11487 through phase-resolved WISE W1--W2 diagnostics
repl.summary: Mid-infrared (MIR) flares provide a direct probe of dust reprocessing in obscured tidal disruption event (TDE) candidates when the primary optical or ultraviolet flare is weak, missed, or strongly attenuated. We present a phase-resolved analysis of the WISE/NEOWISE W1-W2 evolution of the MIR-selected TDE candidate UGC 11487/WTP14adeqka over 2014-2024. We combine timing, colour, and flux diagnostics with phenomenological modelling, hydrodynamically motivated clumpy dust-echo calculations, and an aperture-matched ultraviolet-to-radio spectral energy distribution of the host. The decade-long flare shows a delayed and broader W2 response, colour hysteresis, and cooling from approximately 900 K to 500-600 K. Positive-fluence centroids yield a preferred delay of $224 +/- 45$ d, corresponding to $0.188 +/- 0.038$ pc. The effective infrared luminosity peaks at approximately $3 x 10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and the integrated infrared energy is $(2.9-3.8) x 10^{51}$ erg. A single self-similar MIR response is strongly disfavoured, with Delta BIC = 281.7, while the preferred compact description is a two-component phenomenological model. Representative hydro-clumpy calculations reproduce the empirical diagnostics in a structured, multi-zone dust-response scenario. The host is a moderately star-forming isolated barred disc without a dominant persistent active galactic nucleus component. These results support an obscured TDE-like accretion transient reprocessed by structured circumnuclear dust and show that phase-resolved WISE diagnostics can recover characteristic sub-parsec response scales in obscured accretion-powered nuclear transients.

repl.title: Geometrical and Optical Design of the GUEST Laser-Ranged Test Masses for the Detection of Gravitational Waves in the $μ$Hz range
repl.summary: The GUEST (Gravitational Universe Exploration with Satellite Tracking) mission aims at detecting gravitational waves in the yet almost unexplored $\mu$Hz frequency range through high-precision orbital tracking. The unprecedented scientific objectives of this experiment demand equally advanced optical solutions: the highly eccentric orbit imposes dual measurement regimes; a low-velocity, long-range scenario at apogee and a high-velocity, short-range scenario at perigee. The substantial disparity between these conditions is addressed through a novel optical architecture incorporating two distinct types of Corner-Cube Retroreflectors (CCRs) with 1" and 2" apertures (CCR1 and CCR2, respectively). The proposed layout has been designed to ensure isotropy and homogeneity of the optical response while maintaining efficient packing over the spherical surface of the spacecraft. The resulting Optical Cross-Section (OCS) has been evaluated using a custom reduced-order model, which captures the behavior of individual CCRs under varying illumination conditions. This model has been calibrated by reconstructing the optical response of the LARES-2 satellite and has enabled a detailed assessment of the contributions of each CCR type along the GUEST orbit. Finally, sensitivity analyses have been conducted to investigate the impact of key design parameters, including the ratio between CCR types, laser wavelength, spacecraft diameter, Dihedral Angle Offsets (DAOs), and mechanical configurations.
